reasoning_content:
WebUI is still downloading the sentence-transformers model from HuggingFace (files like vocab.txt, tokenizer_config.json, train_script.py — the big one being model.safetensors, ~90MB). This is the first startup. The Uvicorn server might not be listening yet because startup is blocked on the download. This download is a one-time thing, and once it's done the WebUI should start up. Let me wait a bit more. The model is all-MiniLM-L6-v2, totaling about 90MB. The download speed seems fine.

Note: the WebUI container's `OLLAMA_BASE_URL` is http://localhost:11434, but no Ollama service exists in this compose setup (as far as I've seen). Let me check whether an ollama service exists somewhere. When I grepped earlier, I didn't find an "ollama:" service definition in the yml. Let me re-check whether the backend automatically starts ollama... Actually, the local-dev profile has AUTO_DOWNLOAD=true, OLLAMA_MODEL=gemma3:1b. The WebUI connects to Ollama at localhost:11434 (from the WebUI container's perspective, is that the host? No — "localhost" inside a container refers to the container itself, not the host, unless network_mode is host). Hmm, docker-compose-ai.yml has OLLAMA_BASE_URL: http://localhost:11434. In a normal bridge network container, localhost:11434 points to the WebUI container itself, not the host. However... the WebUI image is "0.10.2-ollama" — maybe the ollama server is built into that image? That would explain the name: "open-webui:0.10.2-ollama" — a custom/variant image that bundles Ollama inside the container. Let me check: I'll run docker exec workspace-webui-1 to check whether the ollama process is running, and try curling localhost:11434 from inside the container.

The main installation target (TruSpace) is working. The AI part is an auxiliary component. Once the embedding model download completes, I'll check the WebUI's health and check whether ollama is inside the container.
